analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The single added hunk (head lines 1030-1047) describes a new PromptTokenCache in LocalTokenizerBridge, per-prefix-cache-scope reuse of token IDs, and ChatTemplateLoopRewrites. The supplied units are BASE text at 1629-2248, which contains none of the changed lines. I therefore reviewed the patch excerpt plus surrounding base context, and the actual implementation is not visible. No source code, authorization, crypto, or attestation behavior changes in this diff.

Security-relevant claims in the new prose that integration should verify against the real code (not provided here):
(1) The prompt-token cache is said never to cross a cache scope. That matches the coordinator-authored cacheSalt scoping in T-041. If the implementation keys on anything weaker than that scope, it would create a new cross-tenant timing/sharing channel adjacent to SEC-035. This cannot be confirmed from docs alone.
(2) The cache holds prompt-derived token IDs in provider memory, which is within the existing A-001 / TB-003 / T-011 / T-014 memory-exposure posture. It is not a new at-rest artifact as described. If it persisted to disk, T-041 would need an update.
(3) Parallel encoding on up to four cores and sampled background comparisons add availability and CPU cost. The kill switch DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0 is documented.
(4) Rendering via the linear-time ChatTemplateLoopRewrites that must match the served template is a correctness/parity concern. A mismatch could alter prompt tokens, and the doc says reuse is disabled on mismatch.

No concrete regression is supported by the visible evidence. needs_deeper_review is set true only because the implementation files (PromptTokenCache.swift, LocalTokenizerBridge, ChatTemplateLoopRewrites) were not supplied, so the scope-isolation claim is unverified.
